source: Digitised from Fig. 5 of: Fregonese S., Bacca M., 'Piercing soft solids: a mechanical theory for needle insertion', arXiv:2412.09809 (J. Mech. Phys. Solids 2021). Fig. 5: dimensionless critical force Fc/(mu R^2) (y) vs mu R/Gc (x), log-log. Exp. 1 = Fakhouri, Hutchens, Crosby 2015 gel data (paper p. 9: mu = 7.2 kPa, Gc = 25 J/m^2, spherical-tipped needles R = 0.1-5 mm); Exp. 2 = Rattan and Crosby 2019 data. All numbers below are DIGITISED from a raster image, not the authors' tabulated data.
method: pixels at native embedded raster resolution (figure is a 1673x1095 px bitmap embedded in the PDF page 10, extracted with pdfimages; not vector, so no path extraction possible). Axis calibration from labelled ticks (tick-line pixel centres): x px = 184.35*log10(x)+1265.2 (ticks 1e-6 at 159, 1e-5 at 343.5, 1e-4 at 528, 1e-3 at 712, 1e-2 at 896.5, 1e-1 at 1081, 1 at 1265, 10 at 1449.5, 100 at 1634; max tick residual 0.2 px); y px = 952.48-155.02*log10(y) (ticks 1 at 952.5, 10 at 797.5, 1e2 at 642.5, 1e3 at 487.5, 1e4 at 332, 1e5 at 177.5, 1e6 at 22.5; max residual 0.4 px). Exp. 1: each marker (ring + vertical bar + two caps) modelled as a synthetic glyph (ring r 6-11 px, bar 5 px, caps 16x5 px) and jointly least-squares fitted to the blue pixel mask (XOR cost), which resolves overlapping markers; the marker centre is the ring centre (also the 1-px tick in the ring hole); error-bar ends are cap centre lines. Exp. 2: marker centre = centre of the hourglass symbol, caps from the component's top/bottom 5-px rows (3 overlapping markers at x ~ 2.2e-3, 2.6e-3, 3.05e-3 read by hand from ASCII dumps). Theory curves: centre line of the colour-matched stroke, local linear fit over +-30 px, sampled at the listed x. Check overlay.png (digitised values re-plotted over the figure).
uncertainty: about 0.005 decades log10 (x and y) for isolated Exp. 1 markers and theory curves; about 0.01-0.02 decades (2-3 px) for the y values of the overlapping Exp. 1 markers at x >= 0.1 (error-bar ends especially) and for Exp. 2 error-bar ends; x has 184 px/decade, y has 155 px/decade. Theory at x=1 (curves overlap, dashes occluded by others): about 0.02 decades.
licence_seen: arXiv abstract page lists the arXiv non-exclusive distribution licence (arxiv.org/licenses/nonexclusive-distrib/1.0/); no Creative Commons licence link was seen. Only numbers read off the figure are stored here, no figure pixels are redistributed.
notes: Exp. 1: 15 markers resolved, not 16. Marker at x ~ 0.75 (and neighbours at 0.56, 0.66) lie in a dense overlapping cluster; fitted by a glyph model, and the marker at x ~ 0.94 has an error bar entirely inside the ring (its hole is filled by two caps), so its y_low/y_high are about +-2.5 px and weak. A 16th marker fully hidden under others cannot be excluded.
In the cluster x = 0.47-1.12 which cap belongs to which marker is partly ambiguous (caps overlap); y_low/y_high for those 5 markers are +-2-3 px.
Error bars are asymmetric in linear units (symmetric-ish in log), y_low/y_high are the cap centre lines.
Exp. 2: 11 points. Three overlapping markers at x ~ 2.2e-3, 2.6e-3, 3.05e-3 were read by hand.

Theory curves sampled only where the stroke is visible: alpha2 and alpha9 at 15 x values 3e-6..28; alpha3 and alpha5 also included. Curve x range in the figure is about 2.8e-6 to 30. At x = 1 the curves are close and dashed strokes are partly hidden, so alpha3 (11.16) and alpha5 (13.11) at x = 1 rest on 9-14 columns.

The marker 'x' coordinate is mu R/Gc as plotted; no check was made that it equals 7.2 kPa * R / 25 J/m^2 for R = 0.1-5 mm (that range gives 0.029-1.44, while digitised Exp. 1 spans 0.012-1.12, so the actual radii or Gc/mu per point differ from the quoted range).
These are digitised values, a bound from above on nothing: no claim on measurement accuracy of the original experiments.
